name: Gudeg

ingredients.name: young green jackfruit, drained and shredded
black tea leaves in a sachet

steps: Rinse canned or cooked young jackfruit thoroughly and shred the soft pieces with forks. Blend shallots, garlic, candlenuts or cashews and coriander with a little water to form a smooth spice paste.
Heat oil in a heavy pot and fry the paste for 5 minutes until aromatic. Add jackfruit and toss for 3 minutes so every strand is coated.
Add coconut milk, 250 ml water, palm sugar, galangal, bay leaves, salt and the tea sachet. Bring just to a simmer, cover and cook very gently for 60 minutes, stirring occasionally.

Remove the tea sachet. Add tofu and tempeh and simmer uncovered for 25–30 minutes until the jackfruit is tender, reddish brown and the liquid has reduced to a moist coating. Turn the cubes carefully so they stay intact.
Discard galangal and bay leaves. Rest 10 minutes before serving with steamed rice; the palm sugar and slow cooking give gudeg its characteristic sweet, earthy flavour.
tips: Use young unripe jackfruit, not sweet ripe fruit. Tea deepens the colour; remove the sachet before its tannins make the dish bitter.
notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.
